items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to the provision of notice to owners whose motor vehicles are subject to safety recalls
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4296

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to the
provision of notice to owners whose motor vehicles are subject to
safety recalls

PURPOSE:

To require the Department of Motor Vehicles to provide notice to motor
vehicle owners whose motor vehicles are subject to a manufacturer
safety recall at the time of the motor vehicle's annual inspection.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new section
210-a to direct the Department of Motor Vehicles to provide access to
the electronic database of all safety recalls issued by the National
Highway Traffic Safety Administration by including a link to
www.safecar.gov on their website. The department is also responsible
to ensure notice of the availability of this information to the public
and directly to every official inspection station.

Section 2 Subdivision (a) of section 304 of the vehicle and traffic
law, as amended by chapter 608 of the laws of 1993, is amended and a
new subdivision (b-1) is added to direct official inspection stations
to make an inquiry to determine if a safety recall on the vehicle
exists. If a recall does exist they must notify the owner in writing
and make them aware that the recall may be repaired at an approved
motor vehicle dealer at no cost.

Section 3 Contains the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

The number of motor vehicle safety recalls has reached record levels
with more than 800 recalls affecting almost 64 million vehicles
occurring in 2014. Currently, motor vehicle manufacturers are required
to notify the registered owners of vehicles that are subject to a
safety recall and inform them that the vehicle can be repaired at an
authorized dealer at no cost to the vehicle owner. However, consumers
are often unaware that there is a safety recall if they have purchased
a used car as manufacturers have difficulty keeping track of ownership
when vehicles are traded-in or sold to third parties.

This legislation requires that consumers be notified at the time of
their Department of Motor Vehicles annual inspection if their motor
vehicle has been subject to a manufacturer's recall. If the official
inspection station finds that the motor vehicle is the subject of a
safety recall, it will notify the owner in writing on the Vehicle
Inspection Report that the automobile may be repaired at an authorized
manufacturer dealer at no charge to the vehicle owner.

It further provides that the Department of Motor Vehicles shall
promote and provide notice to consumers of the availability of
information on motor vehicle safety recalls. This includes providing a


link on the DMV website to the National Highway Traffic Safety
Administration's searchable database of safety recalls at
www.safercar.gov. By entering their vehicle's VIN number into
www.safercar.gov a consumer can easily determine if there is a safety
recall on their vehicle. The Department of Motor Vehicles is also
required to provide this information to consumers through an insert
included with a motor vehicle owner's registration or renewal.

This legislation will strengthen consumer protections and enhance
motor vehicle safety in New York.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law; provided, however, that
effective immediately any and all actions necessary to implement the
provision of this act on its effective date are authorized and
directed to be completed by the department of motor vehicles on or
before such effective date.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4296A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to the provision of notice to owners whose motor vehicles are
subject to safety recalls

PURPOSE:

To direct the department of motor vehicles to maintain an internet
link of motor vehicle safety recalls, and cause an inquiry to be made
thereof upon the annual vehicle inspection.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new section
210-a to direct the department of motor vehicles to provide access to
the electronic database of all safety recalls issued by the National
Highway Traffic Safety Administration by including a link to
"safecar.gov" on their website. The department shall promote and
provide public notice of this information on their website and on a
separate insert provided to motor vehicle owners upon issuance or
renewal of a registration.

Section 2 Subdivision (a) of section 304 of the vehicle and traffic
law, as amended by chapter 608 of the laws of 1993, is amended and a
new subdivision (b-1) is added to direct official inspection stations
to submit to the department the vehicle identification number at the
time of inspection. The department shall determine if a safety recall
on the vehicle exists by reviewing the NHTSA website" safercar.gov".
If a recall exists, the owner will be notified in writing on the
printed vehicle inspection report. If the owner is a dealer, the
dealer shall provide such vehicle inspection report to the next retail
purchaser or lessee.

Section 3 Contains the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

The number of motor vehicle safety recalls has reached record levels
with more than 800 recalls affecting almost 64 million vehicles
occurring in 2014. Currently, motor vehicle manufacturers are required
to notify the registered owners of vehicles that are subject to a
safety recall and inform them that the vehicle can be repaired at an
authorized dealer at no cost to the vehicle owner. However, consumers
are often unaware that there is a safety recall if they have purchased
a used car as manufacturers have difficulty keeping track of ownership
when vehicles are traded-in or sold to third parties.

This legislation requires that consumers be notified if their motor
vehicle has been subject to a manufacturer's recall at the time of
their Department of Vehicle annual inspection. If the official
inspection station finds through a department check of the NHTSA
website that the motor vehicle is the subject of a safety recall, it
will notify the owner in writing on the Vehicle Inspection Report that
the automobile may be repaired at an authorized manufacturer dealer at
no charge to the vehicle owner. If the owner is a dealer, the dealer


shall provide the vehicle inspection report to the next retail
purchaser or lessee of the motor vehicle.

It further provides that the Department of Motor Vehicles shall
promote and provide notice to consumers of the availability of
information on motor vehicle safety recalls. This includes providing a
link to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's
searchable database of safety recalls on their website safercar.gov.
By entering their vehicle's VIN number into safercar.gov a consumer
can easily determine if there is a safety recall on their vehicle.
The Department of Motor Vehicles is also required to provide this
information to consumers through an insert included with all motor
vehicle owner's registration or renewal.

This legislation will strengthen consumer protections and enhance
motor vehicle safety in New York.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law; provided, however, that
effective immediately any and all actions necessary to implement the
provision of this act on its effective date are authorized and
directed to be completed by the department of motor vehicles on or
before such effective date.
